item.title: The Universe May Have Just Revealed the True Nature of Empty Space
item.author: PBS Space Time
item.content:encoded:
Displate’s offering up to up to for 33% off at: https://displate.com/l/spacetime when you use the code: SPACETIME
Nothing is complicated. By which I mean, everything is complicated, because in physics even completely empty space is described as being full of quantum fields doing complicated things even when nothing else is there. So if empty space has these exotic properties, what sort of crazy stuff can we make it do? One prediction that’s been around for a while is that under extreme conditions, empty space can be sort of crystalized. And there’s good evidence that we’ve observed this for the first time.

item.title: We've Finally Seen a Magnetar Being Born

item.content:encoded:
Have we just seen a magnetar being born? Astrum viewers can get 5% off with code ASTRUM at checkout. https://bit.ly/dwarf-mini-telescope
▀▀▀▀▀▀
In December 2024, astronomers caught a rare superluminous supernova in action, and it did something unexpected. It kept pulsing. Scientists raced to explain what made this cosmic explosion so unusual. Was this our first ever glimpse at the birth of a magnetar - one of the most extreme objects in the universe?

item.title: So You Want to Understand Quantum Mechanics…
item.author: PBS Space Time
item.content:encoded:
Sign Up on Patreon to get access to the Space Time Discord! https://www.patreon.com/pbsspacetime
Spend two hours exploring the strange, counterintuitive world of quantum mechanics, where particles can exist in multiple states, reality becomes uncertain, and observation itself seems to matter. We’ll break down some of the biggest ideas in quantum physics—from wave functions and superposition to entanglement, uncertainty, and the nature of measurement. By the end, you may not completely understand quantum mechanics—but you’ll understand why nobody else completely does either.
